caption: Full adder in a 4x4x4 cube, 36 blocks: two half adders stacked. The bottom one adds a and b, and its sum climbs a redstone dust onto the top one, which adds the carry-in and gives the sum. Each half adder lights its own carry block, and the carry-out lamp sits between the two blocks, so it lights when either carry does. (A glass block above the bottom carry torch keeps that torch from lighting the lamp. w86, 2026-10-21.)

Half adder, 17 blocks (4x2x3): adds two bits into a sum and a carry, found by a SAT search. A torch on input a and input b's wire meet in a comparator that is fully on when both are off, barely on when only b is on and off when a is on; the carry lights when b is on and that comparator is off (both inputs on), and the sum lights when exactly one input is on. (w86, 2026-10-21, `circuit arith synth --r7`.)

Full adder bit slice, 54 blocks per bit: copies stacked every 7 blocks make a ripple-carry adder of any width (judged at 1 to 4 and 8 bits). Each bit is two half adders side by side; each half adder's carry feeds a repeater, the two lines join, and a last repeater lights a lamp that is the next bit's carry-in. (w86, 2026-10-21.)
